content.title: About
content.content: Gordita is a traditional Mexican corn‑maize flatbread made from masa (corn dough) and filled with a savory stuffing. This version uses seasoned beans (3345) as the filling, giving the dish a hearty flavor and an extra boost of plant protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gorditas are commonly eaten for breakfast, lunch or dinner and are designed to be handheld.
Beans are considered a “food of the gods” in Mexican cuisine and appear in countless dishes.
The dough for gorditas is leaven‑free, resulting in a soft yet slightly chewy texture.
Traditionally they are cooked on a hot griddle or open flame, which creates a lightly toasted crust.
The bean‑filled version is popular among vegetarians for its protein content.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The combination of corn masa and beans leads to a slower rise in blood sugar.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beans are a good source of folate and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking beans before cooking helps mitigate this.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Sodium in prepared filling
items.content: If the bean filling is salted, monitor overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the gordita hot, split it open and top with fresh vegetables, salsa, guacamole or sour cream. It works well as a snack or as part of a complete meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared gorditas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in an oven or on a skillet before serving.
